subject: Made-to-measure alcove cabinetry
hook: Straight cabinet, wonky wall. Watch the gap disappear.
ig:
Straight cabinet, wonky wall. The trick to a gap-free alcove unit isn't forcing the cabinet to bend. It's the filler.

How we work:

We measure the alcove at floor, middle and top, because the wall can wander from one to the next.
The carcass is built square and true in our workshop. Square furniture is what makes doors hang straight.
A filler panel is then marked against the wall so it follows every bump and lean.
It's trimmed to that line and fixed, closing the gap along the full height.
Finally, a level check across the top before we call it done.

That's the difference between furniture that looks built in and furniture that looks pushed in.

Got alcoves you've given up on because the walls are all over the place? Comment ALCOVE and we'll send you the link.
fb:
If you live in an older house, you'll know the walls are rarely straight. So how do you get a fitted alcove unit to sit tight against them?

This clip shows how we work. We build the cabinet square in our Hanley workshop so the doors hang properly, then use a filler panel that's scribed to follow the exact shape of your wall. It gets trimmed, fitted, and the gap disappears top to bottom.

It's a small step that makes a big difference to how built-in the finished piece looks.
